about: workflow:find-where-someone-appeared: find where someone appeared, read from the person's own store. It is the store half of tools/know-who-is-in-this: its row for this reading reached records through the records door, which is retired, so the row is deleted and this recipe is its home (rule a-tool-is-only-what-the-store-cannot-do; L101: the recipe reads back first). The prints stay on the device they were made on.

payload.label: Find where someone appeared
payload.job: Read back the rows of where people appeared from the person's own store: every recording and time a person was heard or seen, or the rows a recording holds, or the rows that name words, in recording order, with who and which recordings they name. Rows a later keep replaced are left out unless asked for.
payload.produces: The appearance rows and their tallies, read from the person's own store, proven on example rows in PostgreSQL and a JSON store.

source.from: tools/know-who-is-in-this do-work/where-someone-appeared.mjs (whereSomeoneAppeared) and read-data/appearances.mjs (ROW_TYPE, STATUS), read on trillion-workshop origin/main; the row reached record:appearance rows through the records door, which is retired
source.note: Only the reading is the store's job: a filter, a sort and a tally over the rows. The keeping of the rows is workflow:keep-who-appeared-in-a-recording.

where.description: Where the person keeps these rows: the store's own address

language.description: How that store is spoken to, in its own terms

credential_name.description: The vault name of the login the run uses, when it needs one

steps.title: Read the rows the store already keeps
steps.do: Speak to the store in its own language, with the login under its credential_name, and read the record:appearance rows already kept: each row's person, subject, how, recording, recording_name, start, end, words and status. Submit where they are kept (or null) and how many rows were read.

steps.title: Prove the read-back on the example rows
steps.do: In a throwaway place in the same store, with these made-up appearance rows (id, person, subject, how, recording, recording_name, start, end, words, status): [{"id": "ann-heard-1", "person": "ann", "subject": "Ann Sample", "how": "voice", "recording": "rec-a", "recording_name": "call.mp4", "start": 0, "end": 12.5, "words": "Welcome to the call", "status": "named"}, {"id": "ann-seen-1", "person": "ann", "subject": "Ann Sample", "how": "face", "recording": "rec-a", "recording_name": "call.mp4", "start": 10, "end": 11, "words": "", "status": "named"}, {"id": "bo-heard-1", "person": "bo", "subject": "Bo Sample", "how": "voice", "recording": "rec-b", "recording_name": "other.wav", "start": 1, "end": 2, "words": "Sample room", "status": "superseded"}, {"id": "ann-heard-2", "person": "ann", "subject": "Ann Sample", "how": "voice", "recording": "rec-b", "recording_name": "other.wav", "start": 3, "end": 5, "words": "Sample room opens", "status": "named"}], run these attempts in order: [{"op": "by person, with the tallies", "person": "ann", "tally": true}, {"op": "by recording", "recording": "rec-a", "how": "face"}, {"op": "by words", "words": "sample room"}, {"op": "none given"}, {"op": "by person, superseded included", "person": "bo", "include_superseded": true}]. A search leaves out superseded rows unless include_superseded is true, sorts by recording_name and then start, and a call with no person, recording or words is refused. Then remove the throwaway place. Submit answers, one per attempt in order, which are [{"ids": ["ann-heard-1", "ann-seen-1", "ann-heard-2"], "people": [{"id": "ann", "label": "Ann Sample", "appearances": 3}], "recordings": [{"id": "rec-a", "label": "call.mp4", "appearances": 2}, {"id": "rec-b", "label": "other.wav", "appearances": 1}]}, {"ids": ["ann-seen-1"]}, {"ids": ["ann-heard-2"]}, {"reason": "Give a person, a recording or words to look for."}, {"ids": ["bo-heard-1"]}].

checks.says: Each attempt answers the rows, the tallies, or the refusal the intent gives

values.reason: Give a person, a recording or words to look for.

steps.title: Answer where someone appeared
steps.do: Run the read the request names through the store's own rows and answer it. Submit answer: the rows' ids, the people and recordings tallies when asked, or the refusal reason.
